findings.title: abort() from another thread races an in-flight commit/body write against TinyHttpd finishing the same Response
findings.description: abort() only sets a volatile flag and counts down `ended`; the worker then returns from run() (setCloseConnection + throw) and TinyHttpd completes/flushes the ExchangeResponse, while a core thread already inside commit() (past the aborted check: setStatus/addHeader/getOutputStream) or inside the FilterOutputStream write (past check()) keeps mutating the same non-thread-safe ExchangeResponse buffer. DefaultResponse.abort(error) is public API documented as safe from any thread (e.g. a timer during a stream copy), so this is reachable. Result: unsynchronized concurrent access to TinyHttpd internals (corrupt bytes before close, AIOOBE/NPE in the copy thread) instead of the SPI contract that the concurrent commit/write fails with IOException.
findings.suggested_fix: Serialize response access with the abort: guard commit/write/flush/finish and the worker post-await path with one lock (or an in-flight counter the worker drains before returning when aborted), so the worker does not hand the Response back to TinyHttpd while a core write is inside it; add a test that aborts from a second thread during a large body write.

findings.title: abort() before commit sends TinyHttpd plain-text 500 instead of closing the connection
findings.description: Confirms known shortcut (b). HttpExchange.abort() is specified as "Closes the connection abnormally", but with nothing committed run() throws IOException and TinyHttpd answers with its built-in plain 500 page (not the standard error JSON, no request id, not an abrupt close). The client sees a well-formed 500 for an aborted exchange and the access log (aborted=true) disagrees with the wire. Reachable when a user calls res.abort() before sending anything.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the pre-commit abort path end the connection without a complete response, e.g. commit with setContentLengthLong(1) and flush zero body bytes so TinyHttpd closes on the short body, or track it as explicit debt in the wave-5-6 SDS and pin the current wire behaviour with a test.

findings.title: abort() does not wake a body write blocked in the socket; the worker is held until writeTimeout
findings.description: Confirms known shortcut (b). A per-request abort (user res.abort from a timer against a slow-reading client) leaves the writing thread blocked until TinyHttpd writeTimeout, holding a worker and a connection slot; many slow readers exhaust maxWorkers sooner than expected. Shutdown is unaffected because TinyHttpd.stop force-closes at the deadline.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the documented shortcut but state the writeTimeout bound in docs/api and the SDS; upgrade when TinyHttpd exposes a connection-close hook.

findings.title: headers() is grouped by name, not received order, contrary to the SPI "in received order" contract
findings.description: Confirms known shortcut (b). HttpExchange.headers() promises received order with duplicates kept; TinyHttpd exposes only per-name value lists, so "A:1, B:2, A:3" becomes A:1, A:3, B:2. Per-name order is kept, so header semantics are unaffected; only a raw-headers view and cross-adapter parity differ.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the shortcut comment; document the deviation for the TinyHttpd adapter in docs/api or on the SPI.

findings.title: GsonJsonCodec maps JsonSyntaxException but not plain JsonParseException from custom deserializers, and treats every IllegalStateException as bad input
findings.description: A user JsonDeserializer signalling bad client data with `throw new JsonParseException(..)` (Gson documented way) escapes decode() unchecked and becomes a 500, while Gson own type errors become 400. Conversely the broad IllegalStateException catch turns a programming error inside a custom TypeAdapter into a 400 that hides the bug.
findings.suggested_fix: Rethrow JsonIOException (no-ctor/unsafe errors) first, then catch JsonParseException as malformed input; narrow the IllegalStateException branch to JsonReader "Expected ..." failures.

findings.title: bind(host, port, handler) answers TinyHttpd errors with an empty body labelled application/json
findings.description: The plain overload installs errorRenderer(status -> ""), so JsonErrorHandler sends Content-Type application/json with Content-Length 0 (an invalid JSON document) for e.g. the 421 Host rejection, and logs to a fresh ConsoleLogger. The core uses the settings overload, so only direct SPI callers hit it.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the default ServerSettings error renderer, or skip the Content-Type when the rendered body is empty.

findings.title: TinyLogBridge.isLoggable always true forces TinyHttpd to build every FINE/FINEST message
findings.description: TinyHttpd guards message construction with isLoggable; returning true unconditionally makes it format per-connection/per-request trace strings on the hot path that the app logger then discards.
findings.suggested_fix: Delegate to a level check on the app Logger if one exists; otherwise filter below INFO by default.

findings.title: Wall-clock bounds in shutdown and JVM-lifetime tests are CI-flaky
findings.description: Assertions such as took >= 900 && took < 2500 ms against a fixed Thread.sleep(1500) handler race the scheduler; JvmLifetimeTest also relies on Thread.sleep(1000) before child.isAlive(). On a loaded CI runner these can fail without a product bug.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the lower bounds, widen upper margins (deadline + 3 s), and replace sleeps with latches where possible.

findings.title: Known item (a): Cookie reflection survives R8 but not classic ProGuard class renaming
findings.description: Mostly refuted for R8: CookieFactoryHook uses Class.forName with a constant string and getDeclaredMethod with constant names; R8 rewrites constant Class.forName strings when it renames the class, and -keepclassmembers keeps the method name. Under classic ProGuard without -adaptclassstrings the name is not adapted and the hook fails at runtime. Outside this group files; noted for the A reviewer.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `-keepnames class com.snoworca.naruserve.Cookie` (or fold it into a -keep,allowshrinking rule with the member).
